content_voiceover: This slide covers two more board questions. Question 21 concerns treatment free remission in CML, asking which requirement is not adequate for TKI discontinuation per the Taiwan CML treatment guideline, and the answer is C, patients who failed first line TKI but achieved deep molecular response on second line therapy are not automatically good candidates for discontinuation, because prior TKI failure predicts a higher relapse risk after stopping. The genuinely required criteria include chronic phase only disease, access to a high quality quantitative PCR laboratory, typical e13a2 or e14a2 BCR-ABL1 transcripts so PCR monitoring is reliable, and a sustained deep molecular response of more than 3 years for MR4 or more than 2 years for MR4.5 before attempting discontinuation. Question 22 presents a 45 year old heavy smoking male with essential thrombocythemia, platelet count 2000, JAK2 V617F positive, and a history of hypertension and prior myocardial infarction, asking which statement is wrong, and the answer is B. It's wrong because with an extreme platelet count above 1500, this patient is at risk for acquired von Willebrand syndrome, and starting aspirin without first checking von Willebrand studies could cause bleeding rather than prevent thrombosis; cytoreduction with hydroxyurea should be the priority given his very high risk IPSET thrombosis score, and aspirin needs to be added cautiously. Options A, C, and D are correct, this patient truly is high risk by IPSET thrombosis, smoking cessation and blood pressure control matter greatly, and hydroxyurea induced skin ulcers are a recognized reason to permanently discontinue the drug.
keypoints: Q21 answer C, second line TKI deep response does not guarantee safe TFR candidacy
TFR requires chronic phase, reliable qPCR, typical transcripts, and sustained deep MR
Q22 answer B, extreme thrombocytosis needs von Willebrand workup before aspirin
Very high platelet counts risk acquired von Willebrand syndrome and bleeding
Hydroxyurea induced skin ulcers mean permanent drug discontinuation
keypoint_voiceover: For TFR eligibility in CML, remember chronic phase only, a reliable PCR lab, typical BCR-ABL1 transcripts, and durable deep molecular response, over 3 years for MR4 or over 2 years for MR4.5. And for extreme thrombocytosis in ET, always rule out acquired von Willebrand syndrome before starting aspirin, since untreated it can cause bleeding instead of preventing clots. Also remember that hydroxyurea induced skin ulcers mean permanent discontinuation, not dose reduction.
